title: L5 §1 — Overview & Customs Classification Engine
description:
## Target
`docs/strategy/layers/layer-5-expanded-commercial-intelligence.md` §1 — Overview & Customs Engine

## Source Material
- Research doc §4.5 Customs, Tariff, and Commodity Classification (lines 1215–1603): FULL customs detail — FPO, multi-source recall, 10-digit resolution, measure scanner, trade remedy, exporter rates, compound/specific duty, supplementary units, VAT determination, valuation modes, classification freshness
- Planmaxer customs-classification feedback: FPO as one recall source among several, multi-family expansion, exporter/manufacturer resolution, measure interaction engine, conservative defaults, whitelist analysis with per-category difficulty, CBAM placeholder, evidence-tiered accuracy

## Content to Produce
1. **Layer Narrative** — broader categories, more sources, decision-grade accuracy
2. **Multi-Source HS Classification Recall** — FPO is one source among several:
   - HMRC FPO API: candidate HS codes from product description
   - CPV→chapter priors: statistical mapping from procurement CPV codes to HS chapters
   - Rule-based hints: known product patterns → HS code families
   - Tariff keyword search: text search against tariff nomenclature
   - ATR/codebook reuse: previously classified similar products
3. **Multi-Family Expansion** — expand ALL plausible HS6/CN8 families to ALL UK10 descendants. Never greedy descent (picking single best). Enumerate all declarable 10-digit codes.
4. **Exporter/Manufacturer Resolution** — exporterRateBasis: named_exporter / annex_exporter / residual_default. Default to residual when identity is unverified.
5. **Measure Interaction Engine** — AD/CVD/safeguard/quota don't always stack. Model interaction rules. Apply correct measure set per classification + exporter combination.
6. **Compound/Specific Duty** — preserve expressions (e.g., £X/kg + Y%). Never flatten to single dutyPct.
7. **Supplementary Units** — as first-class requirement. Some tariff lines require quantity in specific units (kg, liters, units) for duty calculation.
8. **VAT Determination** — separate vatRateState + national additional codes. VAT rate determination separated from VAT recovery assumptions.
9. **Valuation Mode** — estimation (1_proxy: inferred transaction value from listing prices) vs declaration (1_actual: with real invoice). Different accuracy bands.
10. **Classification Freshness** — tariffCheckedAt, classificationFreshUntil, tradeRemedyWatchState, daily TRA watcher for changes
11. **Conservative Defaults** — MFN rate (not preferential), residual duty (not named exporter), out-of-quota, standard VAT (not reduced), boundary scenarios. Constitutional invariant.
12. **Customs Branch Divergence** — hard blocker, not scenario band. Materially different tariff branches → CLASSIFICATION_AMBIGUOUS error, not averaged.
13. **CBAM Forward Placeholder** — iron/steel/aluminium readiness for future regulation

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Multi-source recall with all 5 sources described
2. Multi-family expansion principle clearly stated
3. Measure interaction engine rules documented
4. Conservative defaults listed as constitutional invariant
5. Classification freshness system specified

title: L4 §1 — Overview & Sync Engine
description:
## Target
`docs/strategy/layers/layer-4-shared-visibility.md` §1 — Overview & Sync Engine

## Source Material
- Research doc §4.7 Database Architecture (lines 1735–1914): authority matrix enforcement, transactional outbox, push protocol, pull protocol, CAS for decisions
- Research doc §6.3 Security (lines 6135–6201): RLS policies
- Research doc §6.4 Performance (lines 6202–6266): sync performance considerations
- Planmaxer sync-engine feedback: advisory locks, push dispatcher contract, executor identity split, active-writer lease, idempotent CAS, pending intent redesign, generation-based rebuild, logical consistency auditor, schema epoch protocol

## Content to Produce
1. **Layer Narrative** — collaboration infrastructure, sync activation, web portal, validation enforcement
2. **Push Protocol** — transactional outbox pattern:
   - Every push-owned mutation creates outbox entry in same SQLite transaction
   - Push dispatcher: single-in-flight batch, identical-envelope retries
   - Batch boundaries: never cross stage_run_id or schema_epoch
   - Batch contains: content_hash per row, schema_epoch, row_version ordering
   - Remote applies via single transactional RPC: apply_push_batch(batch_json)
3. **Pull Protocol** — cursor-based pull:
   - Pull targets: shared_source_configs, shared_company_profile, operator_decision_heads
   - remote_change_seq serialization via transaction-scoped advisory locks per domain
   - Pull-before-push ordering: pull remote state FIRST, then classify/coalesce pending intents, then resume push
4. **CAS for Operator Decisions** — update_operator_decision(process_id, disposition, base_revision, command_id). Idempotent via command_id. Mismatch → conflict returned (not silently overwritten). Pending intents flushed through CAS.
5. **Active-Writer Lease** — one daemon per org enforced at push protocol level. Second daemon instance detected and rejected.
6. **Schema Epoch** — schema_epoch on every batch. Incompatible epoch → sync pauses, local operation continues. Transition protocol: expand/drain/upgrade/contract (stubbed initially).
7. **Sync Infrastructure Tables** — local_outbox, sync_batches, pull_cursors (CREATE TABLE DDL)

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Push protocol fully specified (outbox, batching, dispatcher, apply RPC)
2. Pull protocol with advisory locks and pull-before-push ordering documented
3. CAS operator decision RPC interface defined
4. Active-writer lease mechanism specified
5. Schema epoch transition protocol described (even if stubbed)

- AC1: Every run manifest is stored as run-manifest.md under the session artifact directory.

- AC3: Daemon-observed facts are recorded separately in the evidence appendix under daemon_observed_* or other machine-authored fields.

L1-FR-ARTIFACTS.8 — Fallback Manifests Exist Even for Failed Sessions
- AC1: If the agent cannot provide a narrative, the daemon synthesizes a machine-authored fallback manifest.
- AC2: Fallback manifests set agent_narrative_missing: true.
- AC3: Failed or interrupted runs never end without either a hybrid or machine-authored run manifest artifact.

L1-FR-ARTIFACTS.9 — Every Skill Run Produces a Hybrid-Authored Run Manifest Contract
- AC1: Every skill execution yields either a hybrid-authored run manifest or a machine-authored fallback.
- AC2: The run manifest is the primary review artifact for later validation and operator inspection.
- AC3: The run manifest is immutable once finalized by the daemon.

L1-FR-ARTIFACTS.10 — Run-Manifest Frontmatter Is Structurally Validatable
- AC1: Frontmatter includes the execution identity, timing, outcome class, item counts, and agent-claimed environment fields shown in this section.
- AC2: Fields whose truth is self-reported rather than daemon-observed use agent_claimed_* naming.
- AC3: Missing required frontmatter fields cause the daemon to classify the narrative as incomplete and fall back or fail accordingly.

L1-FR-ARTIFACTS.11 — Agent Narrative Sections Are Required and Evidence-Anchored
- AC1: The narrative contains Summary, Steps Taken, Decisions Made, Warnings, and Evidence sections.
- AC2: Major claims about page correctness, locale/currency, extraction completeness, and pricing plausibility are anchorable to contract fields, daemon appendix data, or artifact refs.
- AC3: Missing or empty required sections cause the daemon to treat the narrative as incomplete.

- AC2: Appendix values come from observability layers, validated contracts, or artifact metadata rather than agent prose.
- AC3: Later validation logic can compare appendix values to agent-claimed values without reparsing the transcript.

- AC2: Fields that could be mistaken for objective verification are not named ambiguously.

- AC2: Fallback manifests explicitly mark agent_narrative_missing: true.

Strategy: Phase 7 — Runner Commit And Stage Tracking

## Phase
Phase 7: Runner Commit And Stage Tracking (bead 1 of 2)

## What To Build
Job Runner: claim jobs from workflow_jobs, execute via adapter, persist results with commit fence.

### Files To Create
1. crates/daemon/src/jobs/runner.rs — Job claim from workflow_jobs (single-threaded in L1). Read job payload: job_kind, scope_kind, scope_id, skill binding. Invoke adapter in correct mode. Monitor 7-phase lifecycle. Validate result contract on success. Run OQG checks. Commit fence: increment commit_seq in commit_clock on every write. Return visibleAfterSeq in MutationAck. Idempotent acks. Continuation handling: persist committed batches, enqueue next segment with resume token. Error handling: create error manifests, update job status, do NOT advance stage head on failure.

### Job Execution Flow (from spec §2.6 VERBATIM)
1. Claim next job from workflow_jobs (single-threaded in L1)
2. Read job payload: job_kind, scope_kind, scope_id, skill binding
3. Request resource budget from Resource Arbiter (no-op in L1)
4. Invoke Agent Adapter in the correct execution mode
5. Monitor session through 7-phase lifecycle
6. On success: validate result contract, run OQG checks
7. Persist stage outputs in same SQLite transaction: write all output rows with shared stage_run_id, update process_stage_status to succeeded, advance process_stage_heads, populate sync tracking columns, increment commit_seq, return visibleAfterSeq
8. On failure: create error manifest, update job status, do NOT advance stage head
9. On continuation_required: persist committed batches, enqueue next segment with resume token

### Commit Fence Model (from spec §2.6 VERBATIM)
Every successful daemon write transaction increments monotonic commit_seq (stored in commit_clock). After commit, emit db.commit{commitSeq, touchedScopes}. Every MutationAck returns visibleAfterSeq. commit_seq is global to state.db, not per table. Rolled-back/failed writes leave commit_seq unchanged.

## Spec Requirements (Verbatim)
L1-FR-RUNNER.1 — Every Durable Write Advances the Commit Fence
- AC1: Successful write transactions increment commit_clock.commit_seq.
- AC2: After commit, daemon can emit db.commit{commitSeq, touchedScopes}.
- AC3: visibleAfterSeq matches the commit fence reached by the durable write.
- AC4: commit_seq is a single database-wide monotonic counter.
- AC5: Ordering is SQLite commit order.

L1-FR-RUNNER.2 — Mutation Acknowledgement Means SQLite Durability
- AC1: MutationAck.accepted=true never sent for in-memory-only state.
- AC2: Ack emitted only after SQLite transaction commits.
- AC3: Retried acks with same idempotency context create no duplicate writes.
- AC4: Failed/rolled-back writes return no new visibleAfterSeq.

L1-FR-RUNNER.3 — The Job Runner Owns the Claim-Execute-Persist Loop
L1-FR-RUNNER.6 — Failure and Continuation Outcomes Diverge Cleanly
L1-FR-RUNNER.7 — Sync Tracking Columns Are Populated From First Live Write
L1-FR-RUNNER.8 — Job Claims Are Basis-Hash Guarded and Cleanup-Complete

title: L1-16: Stage tracking in runner.rs — stage_run_id scoping, set-replacement vs additive, basis-hash guard, staleness
description:
## SOURCE OF TRUTH WARNING
Spec: docs/strategy/layers/layer-1-thin-local-runner.md §3.3 (Stage Tracking Model)
TDD: docs/pipeline/l1-daemon-core/artifacts/l1-daemon-core-tdd.md §8.3 (E2E-ING-013 through E2E-ING-018)
Strategy: Phase 7 — Runner Commit And Stage Tracking

## Phase
Phase 7: Runner Commit And Stage Tracking (bead 2 of 2)

## What To Build
Stage tracking logic: stage_run_id scoping, process_stage_status, process_stage_heads, set-replacement vs additive semantics, staleness model.

### Implementation In
Extend crates/daemon/src/jobs/runner.rs with stage tracking logic.

### Stage-to-Scope-Grain Mapping (from spec §3.3.2 VERBATIM)
| Stage | scope_kind | Commit Semantics |
|Ingest | (not in process_stage_status) | Source-batched precursor |
|Normalize | notice | Set-replacement |
|Relate | process | Set-replacement |
|Prequalify notice | notice | Set-replacement |
|Qualify lot | lot | Set-replacement |
|Acquire docs | notice | Set-replacement |
|Extract lots | notice | Set-replacement |
|Extract products | lot | Additive |
|Score quoteability | candidate | Additive |
|Price-signal match | candidate_source_pair | Additive |
|Gross margin gate | candidate | Additive |
|Landed cost | candidate_quote_scenario | Additive |
|Net margin gate | candidate | Additive |
|Manifest | process | Set-replacement |
|Operator decision | process | Set-replacement |
|Bid workflow | process | Set-replacement |

scope_kind constrained to: process, notice, lot, candidate, candidate_source_pair, candidate_quote_scenario

### Commit Semantics (from spec §3.3.3 VERBATIM)
Set-replacement: commit atomically for full scope. Partial results stored as checkpoint/debug only, do NOT advance head.
Additive: commit independently per scope grain. Failed siblings do not invalidate committed units.

### Stage Head Advancement Rules (from spec §3.3.4)
1. Set-replacement: head advances only after ALL outputs committed in single transaction.
2. Additive: head advances per individual scope unit.
3. Atomic pair: stage output write + stage_run_id + head advancement in same SQLite transaction.
4. Freshness tracking: freshness_state starts as 'fresh'.

### Staleness Model (from spec §3.3.5)
- Hard invalidation: semantic input changed -> mark hard_invalid -> rerun from earliest invalid stage
- Soft staleness: time-sensitive inputs aged -> mark soft_stale -> keep viewable, block auto-qualification if within 10pp of gate
- Guard rule: every job carries expected_input_basis_hash, mismatch -> mark job obsolete, enqueue rerun

## Spec Requirements (Verbatim)
L1-FR-PIPELINE.16 — stage_run_id Is the Atomic Commit Cohort Identifier
- AC1: One stage_run_id represents one atomic commit cohort for one scoped business unit.
- AC2: A single session may produce multiple stage_run_id values when additive stages commit multiple scoped units.
- AC3: process_stage_status and process_stage_heads treat stage_run_id as the authoritative cohort key.
- AC4: Each retry or rerun receives a fresh stage_run_id; failed or obsolete cohort identifiers are never reused.

L1-FR-PIPELINE.17 — scope_kind Uses Only the Six Canonical Values
- AC1: Layer 1 stage tracking uses only process, notice, lot, candidate, candidate_source_pair, and candidate_quote_scenario.
- AC2: Ingest remains a precursor tracked at job/cursor level until notice/process identity exists.
- AC3: Layer 1 does not invent extra scope kinds for convenience.

L1-FR-PIPELINE.18 — Stage-to-Scope Mapping Matches the Cross-Layer Stage Scope Matrix
- AC1: Every stage in this table uses the same runtime grain and scope_kind defined in layer-strategy.md §10.
- AC2: Set-replacement vs additive semantics match the cross-layer contract for the same stage.
- AC3: Layer 1 does not redefine scope grain for a stage that later layers also use.

L1-FR-PIPELINE.19 — Commit Semantics Distinguish Set-Replacement From Additive Stages
- AC1: Set-replacement stages never advance the head from a partial scope result.
- AC2: Additive stages may leave previously committed successful scope units authoritative while sibling units fail.
- AC3: Checkpoints/debug artifacts from partial work do not masquerade as committed stage outputs.
- AC4: Failed set-replacement attempts leave no orphaned authoritative push-owned domain rows committed under the failed stage_run_id.
- AC5: Additive stages record per-scope-unit outcomes so one agent session can show both succeeded and failed scope units explicitly.

L1-FR-PIPELINE.20 — Stage-Head Advancement Is Atomic and Scope-Aware
- AC1: Stage-head advancement occurs in the same transaction as stage output writes.
- AC2: Set-replacement stages advance only after the full scope unit succeeds.
- AC3: Additive stages advance per committed scope unit.
- AC4: freshness_state is initialized and updated according to the staleness model instead of being left implicit.
- AC5: A rerun inserts a new process_stage_status row with a fresh stage_run_id; process_stage_heads move by pointing to the new successful cohort rather than mutating historical status rows in place.

L1-FR-PIPELINE.21 — Staleness and Basis-Hash Guards Prevent Stale Commits
- AC1: Hard-invalid outputs are excluded from current rollups and trigger rerun from the earliest invalid stage.
- AC2: Soft-stale outputs remain viewable but constrain downstream automation as described here.
- AC3: Every job carries expected_input_basis_hash.
- AC4: Basis-hash mismatch causes the current job to be marked obsolete and replaced with a rerun from the correct stage boundary.

L1-FR-RUNNER.4 — Successful Stage Writes Are Atomic Cohorts
- AC1: Stage output rows, process_stage_status, and process_stage_heads updates commit in the same transaction.
- AC2: The shared stage_run_id is written in that same transaction.
- AC3: A failed transaction leaves neither partial authoritative outputs nor an advanced stage head.

L1-FR-RUNNER.5 — stage_run_id Scope Rules Are Enforced
- AC1: One stage_run_id corresponds to one atomic commit cohort for one scoped business unit.
- AC2: Set-replacement stages require one complete stage_run_id cohort for the full scope before head advancement.
- AC3: Additive stages may produce multiple stage_run_id cohorts from one agent session, one per completed scope unit.

L1-FR-RUNNER.9 — Set-Replacement Partial Success Never Leaks Into Authoritative Heads
- AC1: If a set-replacement stage fails after producing only part of its intended scope, authoritative push-owned domain-table writes from that failed attempt are rolled back from the transaction and remain absent from current stage heads.
- AC2: Salvageable partial data from a failed set-replacement attempt may persist only as checkpoint/debug artifacts or explicit failure context, not as current authoritative stage outputs.
- AC3: A later successful retry of the same set-replacement scope advances the head with a fresh successful stage_run_id, not by reusing a partially failed cohort.
- AC4: The retry inserts a new process_stage_status row with that fresh stage_run_id; prior failed attempts remain audit-visible but are never rewritten into success.

## TDD Verification
E2E-ING-013 (T4): stage outputs, process_stage_status, process_stage_heads, and commit_clock commit atomically. Reqs: L1-FR-PIPELINE.13, L1-FR-RUNNER.1, L1-FR-RUNNER.4, L1-FR-DB.2
E2E-ING-014 (T4): stage-to-scope mapping matches the six canonical scope kinds. Reqs: L1-FR-PIPELINE.17, L1-FR-PIPELINE.18
E2E-ING-015 (T4): set-replacement stages never leak partial writes or head movement. Reqs: L1-FR-PIPELINE.19, L1-FR-RUNNER.9
E2E-ING-016 (T4): additive stages commit multiple scoped units from one session while failed siblings remain explicit failures. Reqs: L1-FR-PIPELINE.16, L1-FR-PIPELINE.19, L1-FR-RUNNER.5
E2E-ING-017 (T4): expected_input_basis_hash mismatch marks job obsolete and enqueues rerun. Reqs: L1-FR-PIPELINE.21, L1-FR-RUNNER.8
E2E-ING-018 (T4): soft-stale vs hard-invalid follow staleness cascade rules. Reqs: L1-FR-PIPELINE.20, L1-FR-PIPELINE.21
E2E-ING-026 (T4): one session exercising both set-replacement and additive proves correct stage_run_id scoping. Reqs: L1-FR-PIPELINE.16, L1-FR-PIPELINE.19, L1-FR-PIPELINE.20, L1-FR-RUNNER.5, L1-FR-RUNNER.9

## Acceptance Criteria
- stage_run_id is allocated per scoped business unit and never reused for failed or obsolete cohorts
- process_stage_status, process_stage_heads, stage outputs, and stage_run_id commit atomically in the same transaction
- Set-replacement stages are all-or-nothing for the full scope and never leak partial authoritative writes or head movement
- Additive stages can commit multiple scope units independently while failed siblings remain explicit
- expected_input_basis_hash guards obsolete work and the freshness model distinguishes soft_stale from hard_invalid
- Only the six canonical scope_kind values are accepted
- E2E-ING-013 through E2E-ING-018 and E2E-ING-026 pass
- cargo check --all-targets passes

## Build/Test Commands
cargo check --all-targets && cargo test agent_procurement_ingestion

### Test Files
Stage tracking is verified by E2E-ING-013 through E2E-ING-018, E2E-ING-026 in `crates/daemon/tests/agent_procurement_ingestion.rs` (created in L1-22).

- `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` on all Rust targets — no unsafe blocks anywhere
- Build gate: `cargo check --all-targets && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check`

- Action: Fail fast; require config review

- Action: Taint browser sessions; create error manifest

L1-FR-ERRORS.38 — HOST_RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED

- Action: May preempt lower-priority sessions

L1-FR-ERRORS.39 — Every Error Manifest Includes Runtime and Resolution Context
- AC1: Error manifests record stage, workflow step, error code, message, and structured debugging context.
- AC2: Runtime context includes CLI vendor/version, adapter version, model/config identity, process IDs, cleanup verdict, last checkpoint.
- AC3: Error manifests link to session artifacts and include next debugging action.

- PRAGMA initialization sequence (from spec §2.7 VERBATIM):
  PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL; PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL; PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON; PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000; PRAGMA cache_size = -64000;
- PRAGMA quick_check on startup
- Store schema_epoch in PRAGMA user_version
- Migration runner: apply 0001 then 0003 in order
- commit_seq increment on every write transaction
- Single-writer enforcement
- Local source bootstrap for `sources`: Find a Tender only in Layer 1, with local runtime config and no `shared_source_configs` dependency

- AC1: All Layer 1 metadata tables live in state.db.

- AC3: Layer 1 does not introduce or depend on a second SQLite metadata database.

- AC1: commit_clock exists as a singleton table with one authoritative commit_seq.

- AC3: Desktop read-your-writes behavior can rely on this fence without routing reads through the daemon.

- AC1: Startup configures WAL mode, synchronous mode, foreign keys, busy timeout, and cache size.
- AC2: Startup runs PRAGMA quick_check before accepting write traffic.
- AC3: The daemon stores schema_epoch in PRAGMA user_version.

|active | Adapter ControlEvent::Started | Same event, phase transition |
|terminating | Daemon session manager | Direct lifecycle frame |
|exited | Adapter ControlEvent::Exited | Translated to lifecycle frame |
|reaped | Session Reaper | Direct frame with cleanupVerdict |
|archived | Daemon session manager | Direct frame with archiveSeq |

### Daemon Crash vs Desktop Restart (from spec §2.8 VERBATIM)
Desktop restart (daemon stays alive): read descriptor, handshake, pull active-session summary, subscribe from last seen seq — streams are resumable.
Daemon crash: PTY master fds die — streams NOT resumable. On restart: detect spawned|active|terminating sessions, kill survivors, synthesize AGENT_DAEMON_CRASH_DURING_SESSION error manifests. Desktop detects via instanceId mismatch.

## Spec Requirements (Verbatim)
L1-FR-DAEMON.10 — archived Means the Session Is Terminal and Queryable
- AC1: All artifacts and metadata for the session are stored and indexed before the session enters archived.
- AC2: workflow_jobs reflects the final session/job outcome by the time the session is archived.
- AC3: No later phase transition is permitted after archived.

L1-FR-DAEMON.11 — Lifecycle Uses Only the Seven Canonical Public Phase Names
- AC1: Layer 1 exposes only created, spawned, active, terminating, exited, reaped, and archived as public session-phase values.
- AC2: Internal drain substates may exist, but they do not replace or invent public phase names.
- AC3: Pre-spawn failures may omit spawned and active because no runtime process ever existed; once a session reaches spawned, it continues through the remaining canonical phases in order.

L1-FR-IPC.3 — Desktop Handshake Negotiates Runtime Compatibility
- AC1: The desktop sends desktopVersion, supported protocol range, expected schema epoch, and lastSeenInstanceId.
- AC2: On successful handshake, the daemon responds with selected protocol version, daemon version, current instance id, schema epoch, commit sequence, health summary, mutation availability, and active-session summary.
- AC3: Protocol-range mismatch returns an explicit handshake rejection and blocks further command use.
- AC4: expectedSchemaEpoch != schemaEpoch returns an explicit schema-epoch mismatch response containing both values and blocks further command or stream use.

L1-FR-IPC.4 — Desktop Restart and Daemon Restart Have Different Recovery Rules
- AC1: Desktop restart with daemon alive allows session-stream resume from last seen sequence.
- AC2: Daemon restart invalidates PTY-stream resumability for pre-crash sessions.
- AC3: On daemon restart, sessions left in spawned/active/terminating are reconciled by descendant cleanup plus synthesized crash error manifests.

L1-FR-IPC.6 — Lifecycle Frames Include Daemon-Owned Phase Transitions
- AC1: Adapter ControlEvents cover adapter-owned transitions.
- AC2: Daemon emits additional lifecycle frames for created, terminating, reaped, archived.
- AC3: reaped lifecycle frame includes cleanupVerdict.
- AC4: archived lifecycle frame includes archiveSeq.

IT-IPC-007 (T2): daemon restart changes instanceId and invalidates PTY-stream resumability. Req: L1-FR-IPC.4

## Phase

## Constraint
#![forbid(unsafe_code)] — if portable-pty cannot express setsid/TIOCSCTTY safely, use a spawn helper binary (L1-FR-PTY.3).

## What To Build
PTY session creation with full session and controlling-terminal semantics.

### Files To Create
1. crates/daemon/src/pty/session.rs — PTY pair creation (master/slave) via openpty(). Child: setsid() -> login_tty()/TIOCSCTTY -> stdio redirect -> exec. CLOEXEC on master fd and all daemon control fds. Record sid/pid/pgid. Default geometry 120x40. write_input() for interactive PTY. resize() for attached sessions. Session lifecycle state machine (7 phases: created->spawned->active->terminating->exited->reaped->archived).

### Session and Controlling-Terminal Setup (from spec §1.8 VERBATIM)
1. Create PTY pair (master/slave) via openpty()
2. Fork child process
3. In child: setsid() — creates new session and process group
4. In child: establish slave as controlling terminal (via login_tty() or TIOCSCTTY)
5. In child: redirect stdin/stdout/stderr to PTY slave
6. Record sid, pid, and pgid
7. Only then exec the agent CLI

CLOEXEC hygiene: PTY master fd and all daemon control fds not intended for the child must be marked O_CLOEXEC.

Fork safety with Tokio: Child-side work after fork() is limited to async-signal-safe operations until execve(). If the PTY crate cannot express the required pre-exec logic, use a tiny spawn helper binary.

Chunked artifact storage at artifacts/sessions/YYYY/MM/<sid>/stream/. stream.index.jsonl with per-chunk metadata (first_seq, last_seq, byte_length, wall_ts_range, sha256). 2. crates/daemon/tests/support/artifacts.rs — ArtifactSandbox: creates per-test artifact root, verifies chunk files, hashes, manifests, cleanup reports.

### Capture Rules (from spec §2.5 VERBATIM)
- Chunks written to temp files, then atomically renamed (crash-safe)
- Hashing is incremental during capture, not computed after the fact
- stream.index.jsonl is append-only during capture, finalized at session archive
- Target chunk size: ~32 KB compressed (tunable)
- Each chunk covers a contiguous seq range with no gaps

### Crash-Recovery Rules (from spec §2.5 VERBATIM)
- Only chunks present under their final filenames are considered durable; temp files are ignored or garbage-collected during recovery
- If daemon crashes mid-capture, already-renamed chunks remain authoritative and trailing open temp chunk may be discarded
- Startup/archive recovery truncates any torn trailing JSON line in stream.index.jsonl and regenerates missing entries from durable chunk files
- Readers must observe only the longest contiguous committed sequence prefix after recovery
- Layer 1 imposes no fixed per-session chunk cap

### Chunk Index Format (stream.index.jsonl)
Each line: {"chunk": "stream/000001.pty.zst", "first_seq": 1, "last_seq": 847, "byte_length": 32768, "wall_ts_start": "...", "wall_ts_end": "...", "sha256": "abc123..."}

## Spec Requirements (Verbatim)
L1-FR-ARTIFACTS.1 — Session Output Lives in the Filesystem Artifact Store

- AC2: PTY and contract-mode captures use the same session-root layout with transport-specific chunk suffixes.
- AC3: Artifact paths are stable enough to be referenced from agent_session_logs and error manifests.

L1-FR-ARTIFACTS.2 — Capture Is Chunked From the First Layer
- AC1: Session output is written as chunk-addressable files.
- AC2: Chunking supports replay, reconnect, lazy history fetch, and gap recovery.
- AC3: The chunking contract is active in Layer 1 and not deferred.

L1-FR-ARTIFACTS.3 — stream.index.jsonl Is the Authoritative Chunk Map
- AC1: Each chunk has index entry with path, first/last seq, byte length, wall-clock range, SHA-256 hash.
- AC2: Sequence ranges are contiguous with no gaps inside a finished stream.
- AC3: Readers can locate capture data by sequence range using the index alone.
- AC4: After crash recovery, readers see only the longest contiguous committed sequence prefix.

L1-FR-ARTIFACTS.4 — Chunk Writes Are Crash-Safe
- AC1: Chunks written to temp files and atomically renamed.
- AC2: Hashing occurs incrementally during capture.
- AC3: stream.index.jsonl is append-only during capture, finalized at archive time.

| clean | All descendant processes exited cleanly before timeout |
| forced | Process group required SIGTERM or SIGKILL |

### Fixed Layer 1 timing budgets
- terminating_grace_timeout = 10s
- drain_timeout = 5s for PTY/stdout drain after exit or hangup

- AC4: The final result contract must be validated if present.

- AC2: PTY sessions may receive ^C before POSIX signal escalation.
- AC3: Cleanup escalates through SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGKILL against the process group.
- AC4: PTY draining continues until EOF or timeout, with EIO treated as expected hangup.

- AC4: The reaper emits cleanup_report.json for every session.

- AC2: forced means cleanup required SIGTERM or SIGKILL.
- AC3: leaked means descendant processes survived the cleanup ladder.

title: L0 §3 — Intelligence Pipeline (Screening-Grade)
description:
## Target
`docs/strategy/layers/layer-0-gold-set-evaluation.md` §3 — Intelligence Pipeline

## Background
The screening-grade pipeline is the core of Layer 0. It runs extraction → matching → cost estimation on curated gold-set data. The pipeline has 15 stages with defined processing logic.

## Source Material
- Research doc §4.1 Procurement Notice Ingestion Sources (lines 473–631): FTS OCDS API, notice data fields, cursor-based retrieval
- Research doc §4.2 Procurement Rules and Notice Semantics (lines 632–724): notice lifecycle, lot structure, CPV codes, NoticeLot entity, three-way relation model (notice ↔ tender ↔ process), amendment handling
- Research doc §4.3 Supplier Price Intelligence (lines 725–1026): matchArchetype classification (6 archetypes), query-wave planning, four-state evidence model, adaptive shortlisting, zero-result recovery ladder, slot criticality, bilingual lexicon
- Research doc §5.3 Canonical Workflow (lines 3113–3271): stage scoping model (referenced, not owned — L1 §3 owns the authoritative scope-grain table)
- Research doc §5.7 Intelligence Pipeline Data Flow (lines 5119–5443): full pipeline stages, qualification, lot extraction, product extraction, quoteability scoring, price-signal matching, gross margin gate, landed cost (screening), net margin gate, coverage rollup
- Research doc Appendix A (Margin Logic): gross margin formula, landed cost components, net margin bands
- Research doc Appendix B (Confidence Model): dual confidence scoring (matchConfidence + quoteUsabilityConfidence), lexicographic gating

## Content to Produce
### Early-Stage Processing (stages 1–6)
1. **Ingest** — source-batched fetch via procurement ingestion skills. OCDS parsing for FTS, HTML/API parsing for CF. Cursor-based incremental retrieval (cursor management in L1 §3). Output: raw notice records.
2. **Normalize** — parse OCDS release packages into canonical ProcurementProcess + ContractNotice + NoticeLot entities. Field mapping: title, description, publishedDate, deadlineDate, estimatedValue, procedureType. Multi-notice handling: amendments update existing processes, new releases create new processes.
3. **Relate** — three-way relation resolution (notice ↔ tender ↔ process). STUBBED in L0: gold set is pre-curated (no deduplication needed). Full engine in L3 §3. Output: linked process graph.
4. **Qualify (Preliminary)** — goods/services/works/mixed classification via CPV code mapping + AI classifier for ambiguous cases. Expiry filtering (deadline > now + buffer). Addressable value extraction (goods-only portion of mixed contracts). Output: QualificationResult per lot.
5. **Acquire Documents** — download tender documents from notice URLs. STUBBED in L0: gold-set documents pre-curated. Full implementation in L1 (live source interaction). Output: TenderDocumentSet with document roles and completeness.
6. **Extract Lots** — parse tender documents into structured lot records. Lot number, title, description, estimated value, CPV codes. Creates NoticeLot entities with lot_cpv_codes junction. Output: per-notice lot set.

### Identity Chain (stages 7–9)
7. **Extract Products** — headNoun extraction, candidateType classification, unit/quantity/specification extraction, matchArchetype assignment (6 archetypes: standard_class_led, dimension_material_led, model_exact, brand_generic, specification_led, commodity_bulk). Output: ProductCandidate per lot.
8. **Score Quoteability** — scoring formula combining: identity confidence, specification completeness, unit clarity, market availability signals. Threshold ≥0.45 for auto-search. SearchProfile creation for ALL candidates (including below-threshold for RFQ re-entry in L2). Output: quoteabilityScore + SearchProfile.
9. **Query-Wave Planning & Price-Signal Match** — matchArchetype-driven wave generation, bilingual lexicon (EN/ZH noun aliases, market framing terms), Chinese retry on Alibaba. Four-state evidence model (confirmed/probable/inferred/absent). Detail-page enrichment with complianceEvidenceTier. Adaptive diversified shortlisting. Zero-result recovery ladder (6 rounds + searchFailureMode taxonomy). Output: SupplierQuote per candidate-source pair.

### Margin Estimation (stages 10–12)
10. **Gross Margin Gate** — three-gate lexicographic confidence (identity → usability → realism). Revenue normalization before gate (convert lot value to per-unit basis). Confidence floors per archetype. Output: CandidatePricingAssessment with grossMarginBps.
11. **Screening-Grade Landed Cost** — HMRC Tariff API for duty (HS6-level, MFN rate), flat freight assumption (single mode), single FX rate (screening). Conservative defaults: MFN rate (not preferential), residual duty (not named exporter), out-of-quota, standard VAT (not reduced). Output: LandedCostEstimate.
12. **Net Margin Gate** — coverage floor (50% netQualifiedCoverageBps). Lot-scoped qualification with qualificationBasis. Output: per-lot net margin bands (low/base/high).

### Rollup (stages 13–15)
13. **Coverage Rollup** (AUTHORITATIVE DEFINITIONS — this section owns these formulas):
    - pricedCoverageBps: (lots with ≥1 priced candidate / total qualifying lots) × 10000
    - landedCostCoverageBps: (lots with landed cost / total qualifying lots) × 10000
    - netQualifiedCoverageBps: (lots passing net gate / total qualifying lots) × 10000
    - unresolvedMandatoryLots: count of mandatory lots without resolution
    - decisionBasisHash: SHA-256 of the pipeline data the operator would review
14. **Manifest Generation** — per-process opportunity manifest from pipeline results (rendering module in L2 §2)
15. **Operator Decision** — approve/reject/watch disposition (local intent queue in L2 §3, remote CAS in L4 §1)

### Supporting Concepts
16. **Bilingual Lexicon** — top 30–50 product families, EN/ZH noun aliases, market framing terms, bilingual unit dictionary
17. **matchArchetype Detail** — full description of all 6 archetypes with example products and query strategies

## Ownership Boundary Rules
- Stage PROCESSING LOGIC (what each stage does) → owned here
- Stage TRACKING INFRASTRUCTURE (stage_run_id, scope grain table, commit semantics) → owned by L1 §3
- Coverage metric DEFINITIONS and FORMULAS → owned here (items 13)
- Coverage metric PRESENTATION → owned by L2 §3

## Acceptance Criteria

2. Early stages 1–6 each have their own content item (not collapsed)

5. Gross margin gate three-gate lexicographic confidence explained
6. Coverage metric formulas included with exact computation (authoritative definitions)
7. Explicit note that scope grain table is in L1 §3

2. **Validation Executor** — spawns validator sub-job as child of worker job (`parent_job_id`, defined in L1 §2 Job Runner). Composes kickoff prompt from: run manifest + `validator-rubric.yaml` (distilled, not raw golden assertions) + structured drift deltas (not narrative history)

4. **Dry-Run Mode** — verdicts logged to scratch tables only. No authoritative rows advanced, no outbox entries, no stage heads moved. Pipeline continues regardless of verdict. Purpose: accumulate corpus for calibration.

7. **Fail-Open Semantics** — validator failures never block pipeline. Worker results advance with `validation_skipped_validator_error`.
8. **Initial Calibration** — calibrate against gold-set manifests from L0. Track false positive/negative rates. Must reach acceptable rates before L4 enforcement.
